name: Toyocho
tagline: Otemachi in 12 minutes and Tokyo in 19 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000.
summary: The station is in Koto City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 12 minutes to Otemachi, 33 minutes to Shinjuku, 36 minutes to Shibuya and 32 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. The station stands -0.8 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 5.3 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at -0.8 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from -1.7 m to 3.6 m, a difference of 5.3 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 3 to 5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 8 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 8 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 8 clinics and 8 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 修世会木場病院, about 15 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 藤崎病院, about 19 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Tozai Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Tozai Line runs at 160% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 木場→門前仲町, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥120,000 to ¥130,000 and 1K ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. 1LDK ¥170,000 to ¥180,000 and 2LDK ¥220,000 to ¥230,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. What holds the figure down: a large projected flood depth and only one line, the {line}, serving the station. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Kiba is ahead on quiet, but Toyocho is ahead on how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Toyocho. It is served by the same lines as Toyocho. To Tokyo, for instance, Kiba is 3 minutes quicker. A one-room flat costs about ¥10,000 more at Kiba. On the number of places to eat out, Toyocho comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Minami-Sunamachi, but Toyocho is ahead on how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Toyocho in a straight line. It is served by the same lines as Toyocho. To Toranomon, for instance, Minami-Sunamachi takes 3 minutes longer. A one-room flat costs about ¥17,000 less at Minami-Sunamachi. On the number of places to eat out, Toyocho comes out ahead.
